sources.citation: Glottolog/hh bibliography entries carrying language code NOCODE_Baonao: Meng Chaoji 2001 瑶族布努语方言研究 (ref 313514, 'Lihu = Nao Klao = Pounou = Baonao'); Chen Meilin 1988 MA Hanoi 'On the White Pants Yao language in Anping' (ref 705559, wordlist, 'probably Baonao'); Đoàn Thiện Thuật, Mai Ngọc Chừ & Pan Meihua 2013 越南瑶语 (ref 569964, 'Báikù yáo yǔ.. probably Baonao').
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Records only; none of the three works could be opened. The two Vietnamese 'White pants Yao' items are attached to Baonao by Glottolog with the hedge 'probably'.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Nao Klao language' (raw wikitext, 2026-09-17); Wikipedia (zh) '布努语' (raw wikitext held by the project under buna1273).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Summarises Meng 2001 only for demography: 28,952 speakers (2001) in Nandan, Hechi, Tian'e and Libo; autonyms pou33 nou22 and [tɔ11] m̥ɔu11 tlou11; representative dialect Lihu 里湖瑶族乡, Nandan. No phonology, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Ratliff, Martha. 2010. Hmong-Mien language history. Pacific Linguistics 613. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nao Klao enters only as 'Yaoli Bunu' (Wang & Mao 1995 point 11), used for onset and phonation comparisons: sec. 3.3.2 'breathy voice.. is rare in category A2, and when present weak: for example, Yaoli Bunu (Wang and Mao 1995:35)'. No Baonao stress statement; only the family-level remark (p.199) that Hmong-Mien nominal prefixes 'are unstressed'.

sources.citation: Schiering, René & Harry van der Hulst. 2010. Word accent systems in the languages of Asia. In Goedemans, van der Hulst & van Zanten (eds), A survey of word accentual patterns in the languages of the world, 509-599. De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: publisher record (DOI); no open copy and no library e-access found (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Lists 'BUNU: Younuo Bunu, Wunai Bunu, Bu-Nao Bunu, Jiongnai Bunu' under Hmongic and gives only the family-level non-statement that Hmong-Mien is usually described as exclusively tonal and that the authors lacked sources; nothing on Baonao.

sources.citation: Strecker, David. 1987. The Hmong-Mien languages. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 10(2): 1-11.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Classification only: lists 'd. Nao Klao (Bunuyu Naogelao tuyu)' among the Pu-Nao subgroup; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page naog1238 'Baonao' (alt. Naogelao, Nao Klao).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Classification comments cite Meng 2001:149-192, Niederer 2002:216 (mutual unintelligibility with other Bunu) and Ratliff 2010; no descriptive reference is attached to the languoid itself. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Zhang Jimin 张济民, Xu Zhimiao 徐志淼 & Li Juewei 李珏伟. 1983. 贵州瑶族的语言 [The languages of the Yao of Guizhou]. 贵州民族研究 1983(3): 189-207.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Survey of all Yao languages of Guizhou from the 1983 Yueliangshan expedition, which covered the Yaoshan (Libo) White-Trouser Yao = Baonao; the only independent (non-Meng) first-hand phonological data on a Baonao variety.

sources.citation: Mao Zongwu 毛宗武, Meng Chaoji 蒙朝吉 & Zheng Zongze 郑宗泽. 1982. 瑶族语言简志 Yaozu yuyan jianzhi. Beijing: Minzu chubanshe. 241 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Standard jianzhi sketch of Bunu (by Meng) with a dialect section that lists the 包瑙 dialect; jianzhi phonology chapters sometimes carry a 轻音/重音 note.

sources.citation: Wu Zhengbiao 吴正彪, Lan Qingjun 兰庆军 & Yang Longjiao 杨龙娇. 2023. 濒危民俗口碑文献的规范化整理：瑶族'冬孟'支系丧葬祭祀辞调查. 华西民俗研究 2023(1). 66 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Long transcribed White-Trouser Yao (Yaoshan/Lihu) ritual-text collection by Bunu phoneticians; likely to open with a phonemic sketch of the variety, the only recent first-hand Baonao data found.

sources.citation: Niederer, Barbara. 2002. Introduction to Chángpáoyáo. Cahiers de Linguistique Asie Orientale 31(2): 211-243.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Open on Persée in a browser (blocked by altcha by automated download); sister-variety sketch cited by Glottolog (p.216) for Baonao's status; may contain prosodic remarks on the Bu-Nao cluster.

sources.citation: Meng Chaoji 蒙朝吉. 2001. 瑶族布努语方言研究 Yaozu Bunuyu fangyan yanjiu [A study of the Bunu dialects of the Yao]. Beijing: Minzu chubanshe. 354 pp. ISBN 9787105046249. Baonao 包瑙 (Lihu, Nandan) section, pp.149-192 per Glottolog.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only published description of Baonao phonology (representative dialect Lihu); the same author's 1985 Dongnu paper treats syllable stress in disyllables, so this book's Baonao 语音 section is the likeliest place for a stress or 轻/重读 statement.

sources.citation: Meng Chaoji 蒙朝吉. 1985. 瑶族布努话连读变调问题初探 [A preliminary study of tone sandhi in Yao Bunu]. 语言研究 1985(1): 215-218.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Abstract explicitly discusses the relation between syllable stress (音节重读) in disyllabic words/phrases and tone sandhi in Bunu -- the closest published Bunu word-stress statement; it is about Nongmo Dongnu (buna1273), so it would supply the sibling catalog entry and the template for what Meng 2001 says for Baonao.

sources.citation: Meng Chaoji 蒙朝吉. 2001. 瑶族布努语方言研究 [A study of the Bunu dialects of the Yao]. Beijing: Minzu chubanshe. 354 pp. ISBN 9787105046249 (中国少数民族语言方言研究丛书).
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Not seen. Douban and CiNii records only (no TOC); held in Beijing public libraries, Shanghai Library and Japanese university libraries; no scan on archive.org, HathiTrust unreachable, LOC has no record. Representative Baonao dialect is Lihu (Nandan); Baonao section pp.149-192 per Glottolog.

sources.citation: NCPSSD (国家哲学社会科学文献中心) search-API results for 包瑙, 瑙格劳, 布努语, 布努, 白裤瑶 (titles/keywords) and abstract searches for 包瑙, 瑙格劳, 白裤瑶+语音/语言, 布努语+重音, 布努语+轻声, 布努+重读, 瑶语+重音, 苗瑶语+重音, 南丹+瑶语, 荔波+瑶语, 冬孟.
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: No journal article on Baonao/Nao Klao phonology exists in NCPSSD: 包瑙 and 瑙格劳 give 0 title hits; the only abstract hits (Lan & Wu 2016; Lan 2021) merely say 包瑙方言 is one of three Bunu dialects with 'no sub-dialect division, small internal differences'. 173 白裤瑶 titles are all ethnographic/cultural except Wu, Lan & Yang 2023. 布努语+重音 and 布努语+轻声 give 0; 布努+重读 gives only Meng 1985 (Dongnu).
